_meta.module: M40 -- can a localised vortex Majorana exist in a NODAL MATBG superconductor?
_meta.claim_class: ANALYTIC DESK CALCULATION on published literature numbers. NOT a BdG solve, NOT a transport simulation, NOT a measurement. Scaling arguments are labelled DERIVED_HERE.

out/m38_vortex.json -- the CdGM route being tested
_meta.materials_correction: arXiv:2503.16410 measures magic-angle twisted TRILAYER graphene (MATTG; theta_top ~ 1.42 deg, theta_bottom ~ 1.55 deg), in a MATTG / 3-layer-hBN / MATTG planar tunnel junction.  paper/DECISIONS_LOG.md attributes it to MATBG.  M38 section 3 gets it right in the prose and wrong in the summary table.

Routes B and C differ by exactly that factor.  The repo's velocity and its critical field do not describe the same superconductor; this is inherited from M38/M39 and is reported, not resolved.

spread_of_the_three_routes.reading: 5 % to 29 % of the normal-state density of states sits at zero energy at the working field.  Every route meets or exceeds the 5 % hard-gap criterion; the measured-extrapolation route exceeds it by 3-6x.

zero_field_thermal_floor.formula: G(0)/G_N = 2 ln2 kB T_e / Delta for N(E) = N_n |E|/Delta
zero_field_thermal_floor.reading: At ZERO field a clean nodal gap PASSES L3 at 20 mK -- 0.9 % (Delta = 258 ueV) or 1.5 % (measured 159 ueV).  The nodal gap is not detectable by a zero-field hard-gap check at dilution temperatures.  The kill is entirely at finite field.

part2_flux_quantum_contradiction.what: whether ANY mesa area simultaneously (i) keeps the nodal Volovik zero-energy DOS below M39's own 5 % hard-gap criterion and (ii) keeps the Little-Parks window above the ~0.5 mT remanent field M39 itself names as the binding instrumentation limit
part2_flux_quantum_contradiction.the_identity: B(L=1) = Phi0/A_mesa is simultaneously the working field AND the width of the Little-Parks window.  Lowering the field to suppress the Volovik DOS narrows the window by the same factor. There is no free parameter.
part2_flux_quantum_contradiction.verdict: 9 of 10 rows FAIL.  The shortfall runs from 1.11x (Bc2 = 180 mT, measured-extrapolation route) to 5.5x (Bc2 = 45 mT, Doppler route). Exactly ONE corner survives -- the BEST measured dome device (Bc2 = 210 mT) on the most favourable of the two routes -- and it clears the remanent floor by 5 %, at a mesa area of 3.9 um^2, i.e. 2.6x M39's. M39's own part-3 table already calls a 0.69 mT window at 6 um^2 'comparable to the remanent field of a large solenoid'; a 0.53 mT window at 3.9 um^2 is inside the same danger zone.  This is a geometric contradiction, not a materials one: it does not go away with a better fridge, a better etch or a bigger f_sat, because B(L=1) = Phi0/A_mesa is both quantities at once.
part2_flux_quantum_contradiction.caveat: The 5 % figure is M39's own rung-L3 criterion, imported unchanged. The 0.5 mT remanent floor is M39's own part-3 statement. This module adds no new thresholds; it only notices that the two are incompatible once the gap has nodes.

part3_majorana_splitting_gapped_vs_nodal.what: splitting of the two-vortex fermion parity mode when the mediating quasiparticles are gapless rather than gapped

rows.law: GAPPED: dE = Delta exp(-L/xi_M)   [M39, xi_M = 49.5 nm]

part3_majorana_splitting_gapped_vs_nodal.reading: The gapped law gives 12 neV at 500 nm; the p = 1 nodal law gives 26.5 ueV, which is 0.51 x the whole minigap -- the parity mode is destroyed outright.  p = 2 gives 2.7 ueV, still 2.5e5 x M39's number but below the 6.1 ueV thermal resolution at 20 mK.  The separation needed to push the splitting under kB*T_e is 7.7 um at p = 1 -- six times the mesa's own linear size -- and 0.63 um at p = 2.
part3_majorana_splitting_gapped_vs_nodal.caveat_flagged: The exponent p is NOT established by any literature this module found.  Sato & Fujimoto give t ~ 1/|r-r'| for IMPURITY-mediated coupling between chiral Majorana EDGE modes in a d-wave Rashba superconductor, and state separately that for an EVEN number of vortices the vortex Majorana 'disappears unless they are separated enough'.  They do not compute the vortex-vortex exponent.  The three values are a sensitivity scan, not a prediction.  NO LITERATURE FOUND giving the vortex-vortex Majorana hybridisation law in a nodal 2D superconductor.

part4_rhombohedral_full_or_nodal.what: is the rhombohedral graphene superconducting gap full or nodal?
part4_rhombohedral_full_or_nodal.answer: FULL on the Fermi surface, IF the pairing is the chiral p+ip that Han et al. argue for.  A chiral p-wave gap vanishes only at k = 0, and the quarter metal's Fermi surface does not pass through k = 0.
part4_rhombohedral_full_or_nodal.status_of_that_answer: SYMMETRY INFERENCE, NOT MEASUREMENT.  No tunnelling or thermodynamic spectroscopy of the rhombohedral superconducting gap exists.  Han et al. list 'determining the superconducting gap symmetry' as future-work item 2 in their own discussion. NO LITERATURE FOUND reporting a measured gap shape.
part4_rhombohedral_full_or_nodal.competing_nodal_proposal: S. A. Murshed, A. L. Szabo & B. Roy, 'Nodal pair-density-waves from quarter-metal in crystalline graphene multilayers', arXiv:2210.15660 -- cited as ref. 26 by Han et al. themselves.  A real (non-chiral) f-wave or a nodal PDW would restore nodes.
part4_rhombohedral_full_or_nodal.finite_momentum_caveat: Intra-valley pairing carries Cooper-pair momentum 2K. Yoon & Zhang (arXiv:2603.16828) show by gauge transformation that this is a chiral p-wave SC on the triangular sublattice PLUS an emergent Majorana crystal on a vortex-antivortex lattice on the dual honeycomb lattice, Chern number +-1, with regions of the phase diagram having NO indirect gap.  See also Gaggioli, Guerci & Fu, Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 116001 (2025).

verdict.headline: The nodal evidence KILLS the TBG vortex route as M39 designed it, and it does not kill it by the route the DECISIONS_LOG assumed.
verdict.not_this_reason: It is NOT true that a nodal superconductor cannot host a vortex Majorana.  Sato & Fujimoto (arXiv:1007.4369) prove the opposite: the PARITY of the Chern number stays well-defined in a gapless superconductor and protects an odd number of Majorana modes at edges and in odd vortices.
these_reasons: (1) Sato & Fujimoto's mechanism requires ANTISYMMETRIC (Rashba-type) spin-orbit coupling plus a Zeeman field plus the Fermi level near an ODD number of time-reversal-invariant momenta where the gap vanishes. Spin-orbit coupling is negligible in graphene -- Biswas, Sensarma & Randeria (arXiv:2606.23994) say so explicitly when constraining moire graphene pairing.  MATBG has none of the three ingredients.

(2) The same body of evidence that shows nodes shows TIME REVERSAL PRESERVED.  Biswas, Sensarma & Randeria: 'there is no evidence for broken TR in the SC state', and a spin-polarised triplet state is inconsistent with experiment.  Nodal AND time-reversal-symmetric means NOT chiral, and Rosenstein's antidot result -- M39's whole hedge -- is a chiral p+ip calculation.

(3) There is no gap for the antidot to lift the core states INTO. Rosenstein raises the charged core states to f_sat*Delta; in a nodal superconductor the quasiparticle continuum reaches zero energy along the nodal directions at every antidot radius, and in a vortex LATTICE the low-energy states are extended Bloch states with Dirac cones (Vishwanath, cond-mat/0104213; Franz & Tesanovic, PRL 80, 4763 (1998)), not localised core levels at all.

(4) At the 2.76 mT working field the Volovik zero-energy DOS is 5-29 % of normal -- M39's own rung-L3 hard-gap kill criterion is 5 %.  And the flux quantum makes the trade all but unsolvable: B(L=1) = Phi0/A_mesa is both the working field and the Little-Parks window, so suppressing the Volovik DOS closes the window by the same factor.  9 of 10 (dome Bc2, estimate) combinations fail; the single survivor clears the remanent floor by 5 % (part 2).

(5) M39's parity device runs at EVEN vorticity (two antidots, two vortices) -- exactly the case Sato & Fujimoto flag as destroyed by nodal-mediated long-range tunnelling -- and the splitting law goes from exponential to power law (part 3).
verdict.the_window: arXiv:2503.16410 is a TRILAYER measurement.  For BILAYER MATBG the direct evidence points the other way: Tanaka et al. (Nature 638, 99 (2025)) fit the MATBG superfluid stiffness to T^n with n = 2-3 and no nonlinear Meissner effect, which they read as a NODELESS ANISOTROPIC gap; and Kim et al. (Nature 650, 592 (2026), arXiv:2505.17200) resolve a single, FULLY DEVELOPED gap with dI/dV -> 0 at zero bias over nu = -2 to -2.25 in MATTG.  The window is narrow, filling-dependent and bilayer-specific.
verdict.the_measurement_that_tests_it: One afternoon, on the M39 mesa itself, inserted as rung L3b between the existing L3 and L4: measure G(0)/G_N through the point contact as a function of B_perp in 0.5 mT steps from 0 to Bc2, at fixed gate. sqrt(B) => nodal => the route is dead; flat then activated => full gap => the route survives.  It reuses hardware L3 and L4 already require and it is the same measurement Park et al. published (their Fig. 5c).
